title: Calculation Note — The Latest-Bill Over-Billed Amount on Residential Natural Gas Supply
content:
**Correct amount and over-billed amount.** For the energy line of the most recent bill on a Residential Natural Gas Supply agreement, the correct amount of that energy line is its billed therms multiplied by the agreement's contract rate, rounded half up to the cent, and the latest-bill over-billed amount is the line's billed amount minus that correct amount when the difference is above zero, and nothing otherwise, and that over-billed amount is what the latest-bill rebill credit returns.

A line whose over-billed amount is not above zero earns no credit. The credit is stated in US dollars and rounded half up to the cent.

### Inputs and their records

| Quantity | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| The energy line of the most recent bill | the energy charge line on the agreement's bill ledger whose billing period starts latest |
| Billed therms and billed amount | that line's therms and amount |
| Contract rate | the contract rate per therm on the agreement record |

### Worked figures (hypothetical line; contract rate 0.7950)

| Billed therms | Billed amount | Correct amount | Over-billed amount | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 112 | 96.32 | 112 multiplied by 0.7950 is 89.04 | 96.32 less 89.04 is 7.28 | 7.28 |
| 112 | 89.04 | 89.04 | nothing | none |
| 112 | 88.48 | 89.04 | nothing (the difference is below zero) | none |
| 75 | 63.00 | 75 multiplied by 0.7950 is 59.625, rounded half up to 59.63 | 63.00 less 59.63 is 3.37 | 3.37 |
